- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent price drop is steep.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 85% of prior peak or 10% below recent high.  
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days after sentiment drop.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; reduce first 5 values by 3–6%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “0.00” values, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to compensate.
